claim: The original (now-abandoned) llm-d RL rollout north-star proposal analyzed five RL frameworks (veRL, Slime, SkyRL, OpenRLHF, NeMo-RL) and found none are Kubernetes-native -- all use Ray as orchestrator -- and none leverage KV-cache locality or prefix reuse in their load routing (best is veRL's SGLang-router + hash-based routing).
stance_target: existing RL frameworks have primitive routing that llm-d's cache-aware scheduling could improve, independent of Kubernetes
quoted_support: All five frameworks use Ray as their orchestrator and manage inference engines as Ray actors. None are Kubernetes-native... Load routing ranges from basic to primitive - veRL integrates SGLang's router and has hash-based session routing, but no framework leverages KV-cache locality, prefix reuse, or predicted latency.

claim: The original north-star proposal explicitly considered and rejected a 'Ray-native rollout service' design, arguing that llm-d should instead 'not take a dependency on Ray's versioning and runtime model' and remain 'consumable from any orchestrator (Ray, bare Python, Kubernetes Jobs) via HTTP/gRPC.'
stance_target: design rationale for keeping the rollout/routing control plane orchestrator-agnostic via a network API rather than embedding into any single scheduler's native actor model
quoted_support: Unlike a Ray-native approach, llm-d RL rollout: Does not take a dependency on Ray's versioning and runtime model; Leverages Kubernetes primitives (LWS, HPA, pod lifecycle) for operations; Is consumable from any orchestrator (Ray, bare Python, Kubernetes Jobs) via HTTP/gRPC.

claim: This entire north-star proposal -- including its full RolloutControl gRPC API (Generate/UpdateWeights/Sleep/WakeUp/GetPoolStatus) and its future RolloutEnginePool Kubernetes CRD sketch -- is superseded; the repo's own README states this direction 'had no active development or users for several months while work moved to the EPP-based routing' and is 'not the recommended starting point for new work.'
stance_target: a bespoke RolloutControl service/CRD is the current recommended llm-d approach for RL rollout routing
scope_conditions: llm-d-incubation/llm-d-rl repo, as of Aug 19, 2026 rename commit and README current as of Aug 31, 2026
quoted_support: It has had no active development or users for several months while work moved to the EPP-based routing above... it is not the recommended starting point for new work.

claim: The proposal defines vLLM's native weight-transfer primitives that llm-d's rollout layer builds on: the WeightTransferEngine abstraction (NCCL backend with packed tensor transfer, layerwise reload with auto-requantization) and HTTP endpoints /init_weight_transfer_engine and /update_weights, gated behind VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE; and three vLLM sleep levels (0: pause scheduling, 1: offload weights to CPU, 2: discard all GPU memory) with tagged wake-up for weights vs kv_cache independently.
stance_target: exact vLLM-side primitives available for building a custom weight-sync/lifecycle backend integration
quoted_support: vLLM already has native support for both via the `WeightTransferEngine` abstraction (NCCL backend with packed tensor transfer, layerwise reload with auto-requantization) and HTTP endpoints (`/init_weight_transfer_engine`, `/update_weights`) behind `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE`... vLLM provides three sleep levels (0: pause scheduling, 1: offload weights to CPU, 2: discard all GPU memory) and tagged wake-up (weights, kv_cache independently).
